vision: Krans becomes the evidence layer that corporate venture teams and the agencies who build for them run their validation on: every call reviewed within minutes, every learning graded and cited, and at the end of each sprint a verdict the sponsor can check, delivered as much through the assistant people already work in as through the app.

strategy.direction: Sell the sprint verdict, not the portfolio dashboard. Package Krans as a priced validation sprint for corporate venture teams and innovation agencies, whose sponsors already pay for validation, and make its output a sponsor-ready go, pivot or kill report cited to the call and second. Make the MCP connector as reliable as the app, because the heaviest users live in Claude, and keep Reflections free as the hook that gets every call into Krans. Hold the studio-wide portfolio overview until one partner uses it across their own live ventures.
why: Nobody in 78 relevant calls is shown paying or signing. The only budgets that moved belong to teams with a sponsor: an innovation agency agreed a four-month pilot verbally and plans to pass the cost to its corporate client, and a corporate innovation team used a Krans prompt to write its sponsor report.

Studios anchor far below the list price of about 3,000 to 4,000 a month: 600 euros for three months, 5,000 to 10,000 dollars for an experiment, or zero while fundraising. Several build their own second brain in Git, Claude or a portal instead.

The three accounts with real use all work through an assistant: the investor briefs himself in Claude before founder meetings, the corporate lead writes Notion pages from Claude, the agency connected Read AI and Claude and cancelled Otter. When the connector breaks, the product is gone for them.

Reflections is the feature users name unprompted, because it changes how they interview; Threads and the baseline come next. The E0 to E5 scale is valued when it is explained and resented when a score moves without a reason.

In the market, recording is becoming free (Notion, ChatGPT Record, Superhuman buying Fathom) and every note-taker now ships an MCP server, so capture is not a moat. The unmet complaint is the step from insight to decision: one reviewer can find the call where pricing came up, not the one where it was decided.
notNow: A portfolio overview sold to studio partners as monitoring. Partners ask for visibility in 15 calls, but investors and a fund partner warn founders will resist being listened to, and no partner has used the overview across their own live ventures.
A standalone note-taker or bot. Capture is commoditised and platforms are blocking bots; Krans should read Read AI, Granola, Fathom, Meet and uploads rather than compete with them.
Outreach and go-to-market automation for founders. Several inbound founders wanted it, but it is a different product and those founders had no budget.
Selling to solo founders. The team itself says they will not pay even 100 a month, and the heaviest founder use was free.

sequence.step: Fix the MCP connector: tools always exposed, no silent logouts, a health check the user can see, and a regression test per release.
Write the verdict report by hand from Krans data for the agency pilot and the corporate team, and ask each sponsor to read it.
Put a price on the sprint (per venture, per sprint, unlimited readers) and send it to the agency, the corporate team and two corporate venture studios from the pipeline.
Productise the verdict and the method editor once two sponsors have used a report in a real decision.
Revisit the portfolio overview with the first studio that runs three or more ventures on Krans.

killCriteria: By 15 December 2026 no sponsor has read a verdict report and no team has paid for a second sprint: the sponsor wedge is wrong.
The agency pilot does not convert to a signed, paid agreement by the end of its sprint.
Users keep choosing their own Claude plus note-taker setup over the connector even after it is reliable: Krans is a feature of their assistant, not a product.
evidenceGaps: No contract, invoice or renewal in any call: whether the corporate team and the agency pay rests on the team's own statements. Check the books before anything else.
No usage data: weekly active users, calls per workspace, and whether use survives the first venture.
The founder-resistance objection is untested outside the studio's own programme. Ask three portfolio founders at a customer before building partner views.
No lost-deal reasons and no head-to-head against Dovetail, Granola or Notion AI.
Nothing yet on what sponsors do with a report: whether they read it, trust it, or ask for slides.
Reddit, X and LinkedIn were not reachable for this research, so the voice of the market leans on Hacker News, Trustpilot, Capterra and Product Hunt.

patterns.title: The winners in capture grew on free, then moved into context
patterns.text: Granola (valued at 1.5 billion dollars in March 2026), Fireflies (1 billion via a tender in 2025), Otter (100 million ARR) and Read AI grew bottom-up on free tiers, then added team spaces, email and MCP. Gong still passed 300 million ARR by selling deal intelligence to revenue teams rather than recordings.

patterns.title: Research tools that charge readers lose to ones that charge producers
patterns.text: Condens charges per contributor with unlimited viewers; Dovetail dropped published seat pricing, and reviewers describe a near 4x tier jump. Studios and corporate teams have many readers (partners, sponsors) and few people running calls, so seat pricing punishes exactly the audience Krans needs.

initiatives.title: Make the connector as reliable as the app
initiatives.summary: Treat the MCP server as the main interface: tools always exposed, no silent logouts, a visible health check, graded and cited answers by default, write-back to Notion, and a regression test on every release.
initiatives.bet: We believe that the heaviest users will live in Claude and Codex, so a connector that never breaks and returns graded, cited evidence will keep them and set Krans apart from note-taker MCPs that return summaries. We will know when connector incidents reported in calls drop to zero for a month and weekly MCP sessions per active account grow.
initiatives.problem: The three real accounts work through an assistant. The connector shows as connected with no tools, loses transcript access, logs users out and must be re-added after releases, and the assistant sometimes answers from Notion instead of Krans.
risks: Better MCP makes Krans easier to treat as a feature of someone else's assistant. Keep Reflections, the verdict and the method in Krans itself.
Assistant vendors change connector rules often; budget for it rather than treat it as a one-off fix.
Corporate IT may block custom connectors entirely. Keep the manual upload and the app path working.

initiatives.title: Price per sprint, unlimited readers
initiatives.summary: Replace the monthly per-workspace fee with a fixed price per venture per sprint (for example six to eight weeks), unlimited readers for partners and sponsors, and read-only access after the sprint ends.
initiatives.bet: We believe that a sprint price that maps onto how agencies and corporate teams already budget validation will close faster than a monthly fee. We will know when two of the next five proposals are accepted without a price negotiation.
initiatives.problem: No studio has accepted the list price; agencies want to pass the cost to a client for a fixed piece of validation; readers such as partners and sponsors should not cost a seat; studios want to keep access to killed ventures.
